name: Goodwill · Karaṇīya Metta Sutta (Sn 1:8)

summary.text: A short goodwill reflection from the Karaṇīya Metta Sutta: may all beings be happy at heart, whatever they are; let no one wish another to suffer; guard this goodwill as a mother guards her only child, and let it go out without limit, above, below and all around.

steps.text: Any posture (standing, walking, sitting, lying down), as long as you are not drowsy.
Think: happy, at rest, may all beings be happy at heart.
Whatever beings there may be, weak or strong, seen or unseen, near or far, born or seeking birth: may all be happy at heart.
Let no one deceive or despise another, or wish another to suffer.
Guard this goodwill as a mother guards her only child.
Goodwill for the entire cosmos, without limit: above, below, all around, without hostility or hate.

max_hold_s.note: no breath instruction at all; natural breath

sources.cite: Karaṇīya Metta Sutta (Sn 1:8 = Khp 9), tr. Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu, dhammatalks.org (also Sutta Nipāta: The Discourse Group, rev. 2017)
